cases.title: Give a joiner access and remove a mover’s old permissions
cases.scenario: HR moves a finance analyst into sales. She needs CRM access on Monday, and her old ability to approve payments should end.
cases.owner: HR owns the employment event. IAM owns provisioning. Finance and the CRM owner confirm the actual permissions.
cases.proof: Start with the role change and follow it into both applications. Time how long necessary access takes to appear and obsolete access takes to disappear. Record connector failures separately.
cases.gap: An identity-provider group changed, but a local finance entitlement survived.

cases.title: Decide how an employee proves their identity
cases.scenario: A contractor uses a personal device to sign in to payroll. The customer wants phishing-resistant authentication for that application.
cases.owner: The IAM owner sets sign-in policy. The payroll owner and help desk own exceptions and account recovery.
cases.proof: Demonstrate the intended authenticator, a disallowed fallback and a recovery path using test identities. Record the application policy that made the decision.
cases.gap: An enrollment percentage leaves open whether payroll sign-in and account recovery actually enforce the required method.

cases.title: Prove that sensitive access is still justified
cases.scenario: A controller finds a former approver on the payment-release list during a quarterly review. Who can remove that permission and prove the change?
cases.owner: The application owner certifies business need. The IGA team runs the review and reconciles the result.
cases.proof: Follow one denied entitlement from the reviewer’s decision through remediation to a fresh target-system entitlement record. Track decisions awaiting action.
cases.gap: A completed campaign can still include work waiting on an application owner.

cases.title: Grant production admin access for a limited time
cases.scenario: An engineer needs elevated access during an outage. Who approves the grant and verifies when the privilege ends?
cases.owner: Cloud IAM and the production owner define eligible roles, approval rules and emergency exceptions.
cases.proof: Show the requester, approved role and resource, start and end times, and effective access after expiry. Check permanent grants separately.
cases.gap: An expired temporary role can coexist with standing privileges granted through another path.

cases.title: Remove a departing contractor’s access
cases.scenario: A contractor’s directory account is disabled Friday. A SaaS session is still open, and an integration key they once administered still has an owner to be assigned.
cases.owner: HR or the sponsor supplies the end time. IAM handles the directory. The app owner handles sessions and the service owner takes custody of the integration.
cases.proof: Reconcile accounts and app-issued sessions at the target. Assign a new owner to shared integrations and document whether each credential needs revocation or rotation.
cases.gap: An identity-provider sign-out can leave an app-issued session alive. A service credential may belong to the integration after its human owner leaves.

cases.title: Investigate an employee credential reported outside the company
cases.scenario: A breach-monitoring alert names an employee email. Is the account active, and was there a suspicious sign-in or a surviving session?
cases.owner: Threat intelligence supplies the observation. The SOC checks sign-in activity. IAM and application owners contain affected access.
cases.proof: Correlate the identity and observation time with account status, sign-in evidence and session actions. Record the log coverage and the period reviewed.
cases.gap: A matching email alone cannot establish that the current password was exposed or that someone signed in.
